snippet.description:
Working full-time while preparing for UPSC Mains 2027? Struggling to balance your job, GS, Optional, and answer writing with limited time?

In this video, Sonia Ma’am shares a practical 3-month time management strategy for working professionals preparing for UPSC CSE 2027. Learn how to prioritise high-value Mains topics, make the most of your morning and evening study hours, and use short breaks for revision and recall.

Book 1:1 Mentorship with Sonia Ma'am: https://shorturl.at/Z7jBL

Enroll in Mains Master Program 2027: https://www.levelupias.com/courses/upsc-gs-mains-master-program-mmp/

Enroll in LevelUp Mentorship Program 2027 (LMP): https://www.levelupias.com/courses/upsc-cse-ascend-levelup-mentorship-program-lmp-ascend/

Previous Sessions Link:
Video 1: Last 7 Months Strategy For UPSC CSE 2027 | Mains + Prelims Strategy
Watch here: https://youtu.be/RiSqMi6ZWfY?si=qZzdHR_5E8FmLga5

Video 2: 80-Day Plan to Cover GS Mains Before December | UPSC Mains 2027
Watch here: https://youtu.be/kl47gluMfr8?si=Bci7rq-MWp13idtU

Video 3: 80-Day Comeback Plan for UPSC CSE Mains 2027
Watch Here: https://youtu.be/RdDzx9FjXU0

In this video, you’ll learn:
- How to manage UPSC preparation alongside a full-time job.
- How to prioritise GS and Optional topics based on weightage and your preparation level.
- How to balance self-study, classes, revision, and answer writing.
- How to plan specific daily targets and keep your resources limited.
- How to track progress without comparing yourself with full-time aspirants.

You don’t need to copy a full-time aspirant’s routine. You need a realistic, consistent strategy that helps you make the most of the time available.

snippet.description:
Preparing for UPSC CSE 2028 while attending college or working a full-time job? How much time do you really need for UPSC preparation?

In this Short, learn why 4–5 hours of focused study every day can help you follow a structured two-year UPSC preparation strategy. The roadmap focuses on completing GS preparation by June, prioritising Optional from June to December, and shifting focus back to Prelims preparation from January.

The key is consistency, realistic planning, and making the most of your available time.
